### BioVie Presents New Biomarker Data from the ADDRESS-LC Trial of Bezisterim in Long COVID at the NIH RECOVER-TLC Third Annual Workshop


November 9, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/104783765/files/doc_news/BioVie-Presents-New-Biomarker-Data-from-the-ADDRESS-LC-Trial-of-Bezisterim-in-Long-COVID-at-the-NIH-RECOVER-TLC-Third-Annual-Workshop-2026.pdf)


*New findings from the Phase 2 ADDRESS-LC trial suggest two distinct biomarker-defined Long COVID endotypes* *1* *associated with different patient responses to bezisterim treatment.*


*Patients with a high-inflammatory endotype showed improvements in objective cognitive impairment, while those with a low-myeloid endotype experienced improvements in fatigue and post-exertional malaise.*


CARSON CITY, Nev., Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BioVie Inc. (NASDAQ: BIVI) (“BioVie” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage company developing innovative drug therapies for neurological and neurodegenerative diseases, today announced new biomarker findings from the ADDRESS-LC trial of bezisterim were presented at the 2026 RECOVER–Treating Long COVID (RECOVER-TLC) Hybrid Workshop. The workshop was hosted by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health (FNIH) from November 4–5, 2026, in Bethesda, Maryland. The RECOVER-TLC Initiative was launched to accelerate the development of treatments for Long COVID. To date, RECOVER-TLC has advanced four therapeutic candidates into clinical testing and continues to evaluate additional promising interventions for this underserved patient population.


Dr. Penelope Markham, BioVie’s Senior Vice President and Program Lead for Long COVID presented *“Learnings from ADDRESS-LC and Implications for Future Trials in Long COVID,”* highlighting the identification of two biologically distinct endotypes with different treatment response profiles. Participants with a high-inflammatory endotype demonstrated the greatest treatment-associated improvement in objective clinical measures of cognition, while those in a less inflamed, low-white-blood-cell (WBC)/low-myeloid endotype demonstrated treatment-associated improvements in fatigue and PEM.


“One of the challenges in Long COVID research is that patients have different underlying biology and may respond to treatment in different ways,” said Penelope Markham, PhD, who leads BioVie’s Long COVID clinical development program. “Our exploratory biomarker findings suggest that treatment responses may vary across patient subgroups and clinical measures, including cognition, fatigue, post-exertional malaise, and physical function. When these populations are analyzed together, potentially meaningful treatment effects may be obscured. This highlights the importance of aligning clinical endpoints with the biology of the patients being studied, in addition to selecting the right participants for enrollment. While preliminary, these insights may help inform the design of future Long COVID studies.”


“There are no established biomarkers for Long COVID,” said Joseph Palumbo, MD, BioVie’s Executive Vice President of Research & Development and Chief Medical Officer. “Previously reported data from the ADDRESS-LC trial showed statistically significant improvements among bezisterim-treated patients with high baseline cognitive impairment, fatigue, and/or post-exertional malaise (PEM) in exploratory analyses. These new biomarker findings provide a potential biological explanation for those clinical responses and are consistent with our understanding of how bezisterim may modulate inflammation and myeloid function.”


**Two Endotypes, Two Response Profiles**


The high-inflammatory endotype was characterized by higher serum amyloid A1 (SAA1), greater IL-6/myeloid activity, and higher hs-CRP and body mass index (N = 67). In this group, bezisterim was associated with a large effect on objective global cognition at Week 12 (Cohen’s *d* ≈ 0.83; p=0.001) while the total trial population and other endotype groups did not experience such improvements.


Figure 1.


Two biomarker-defined endotypes associated with differential efficacy profiles


The low-WBC/low-myeloid endotype (N = 44) included participants outside the higher-SAA1 group with lower neutrophil and monocyte levels. In this group, bezisterim was associated with effects across PROMIS Fatigue and DSQ-PEM (Cohen’s *d* ≈ 0.80 to 0.90; p≈0.11).


The analyses suggest that a single efficacy endpoint may not adequately capture clinically meaningful response to a therapeutic intervention across the biological diversity of Long COVID. Objective measures of cognition may be particularly informative in patients with high inflammation, whereas fatigue, PEM and physical function may be more relevant endpoints for a low WBC/low-myeloid population. Greater baseline symptom severity may help identify patients most likely to demonstrate measurable improvements in corresponding outcomes, supporting a future design that integrates biological and clinical enrichment strategies.


The ADDRESS-LC evaluated 380 different plasma biomarkers. Across the analyzed population, neuropeptide Y (NPY), a biomarker shown previously to be significantly elevated in patients with Gulf War Syndrome and ME/CFS,2 significantly decreased with bezisterim, with a Week 12 treatment contrast of approximately 33% lower relative abundance.


Additional data will be presented at the upcoming 4th Long COVID International Conference 2026 to be held in Nice, France from November 12-13, 2026.


**Relationship to Previously Reported Findings**


The ADDRESS-LC trial randomized 203 participants to receive either bezisterim 20 mg twice daily or matched placebo for 12 weeks. In the overall population, bezisterim showed a consistent trend toward improvement across both objective and patient-reported efficacy outcomes but none reached statistical significance. Previously reported pre-specified exploratory subgroup analyses showed that participants with greater baseline fatigue, PEM or cognitive impairment experienced greater treatment benefits, including statistically significant improvement in multiple measures corresponding to their most pronounced baseline symptoms. The newly reported endotype analyses provide additional biological context for these distinct patterns of treatment response.


Bezisterim demonstrated a safety and tolerability profile comparable to placebo. Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 41.6% of bezisterim-treated participants compared with 55.9% of placebo-treated participants. No deaths occurred, and no serious treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in the bezisterim group.


**About Long COVID**


An estimated 17-20 million U.S. adults reported to be living with Long COVID,3 with 3.8 million experiencing significant limitation to their daily lives.4 Almost 50 percent of those with Long COVID develop persistent or intermittent symptoms.5 The neurological and neuropsychiatric symptoms are among the most common and disabling manifestations of the condition and include fatigue, PEM, sleep disturbance, and persistent sense of difficulty with thinking and memory.6 Chronic innate inflammation accompanied by ongoing immune dysregulation is among the leading hypotheses proposed to explain the symptoms in Long COVID, with numerous investigators describing findings in Long COVID that appear to be supportive of the intended biological targets of bezisterim. Currently, there are no FDA-approved treatment options for Long-COVID.


**About the ADDRESS-LC trial**


The Phase 2 ADDRESS-LC study ([NCT06847191](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=tZGcvlNENEN4OpVK6dr3246rzIw7AApQVnE_HKIIz4g126kg46gzI_oA4VW1BUhTR9h6ow_u62xXjX5SFPsMBon7BPNc2JvCRuzKnp1qXhkwEyU9hV2t4bs4vxgWTllqrNbgK5N62dTlax197z9UE01f4OEpBWcQ5Sv6b3SmMTFohB17LjhspdeQ5S00EnLp6bqlFSJNj719Is-3H_Kf5G6zbIbaeTgSCeIpQ2THA6IP4vQ0z0qR00EQVTUfyFc_-uIxTWSqSovLsbKVzJRoObvJ0d_QLG-oA8WZab0pKyrDlb6Fi79FKmOqfZXQqBD3Qa_Ky1zaVRzMGP22DeEh8JG_ZgUmcPfTiOdEV9Z1vjtaPdBo_vNvLC_jHhtdMRog_oYVssyhizV49MhwXg7RVKBulktyfyo9r_uVU1P2qnYxnZmeA8OEqykbkhqMrBJUFn68fOs8k2dF70gyqjVBXdy4YLFZUpteljFN98iS__A=) ), which is fully funded by a grant from the U.S. Department of War (DoW), is a randomized (1:1), placebo-controlled, signal-finding proof-of-concept, multicenter trial evaluating the efficacy, safety and tolerability of bezisterim in adult participants with Long COVID who have cognitive impairment sequelae and fatigue. The study compared bezisterim, administered as a 20 mg oral capsule twice daily, with a matching placebo to assess its effects on neurocognitive and fatigue-related symptoms. The trial evaluated 22 clinical outcome measures, with no single endpoint pre-specified as the primary determinant of study success. Endpoints include assessing changes in overall clinical benefit, subjective and objective cognitive function, fatigue, sleep disturbance, Quality of Life and PEM. As a signal-finding study, the trial was designed to identify efficacy signals, measure treatment effect magnitude, and identify patient subgroups most likely to benefit, to inform the design of future Phase 3 trials.


**About Bezisterim**


Bezisterim (NE3107) is an investigational oral drug that crosses the blood-brain barrier and works to reduce inflammation and improve insulin sensitivity without suppressing the immune system and with a low risk of drug-drug interactions. By modulating key pathways involved in neuroinflammation (ERK, NFκB, TNFα), bezisterim may have therapeutic potential in several disease indications, including Parkinson’s disease (PD), Long COVID (LC), and Alzheimer’s disease (AD).


In PD, BioVie completed the SUNRISE-PD trial, which enrolled 57 patients to establish proof of mechanism and proof of concept in individuals with early-stage disease who had not previously been treated with carbidopa/levodopa. Topline results showed that patients treated with bezisterim experienced improvements with blood-based markers of inflammation, as well as a broad range of biomarkers associated with cellular health and neuronal integrity. Clinically, patients treated with bezisterim showed numerically greater improvements than those receiving placebo across multiple measures of daily functioning, motor symptoms, and non-motor symptoms.


For LC, the ADDRESS-LC trial enrolled approximately 200 patients to evaluate whether bezisterim may help reduce brain fog, fatigue, and other lingering neurological symptoms associated with LC. The hypothesis being studied is that these symptoms may be triggered by persistent circulation of spike protein fragments that trigger inflammation via NFκB activation (which bezisterim has been shown to modulate).


In AD, BioVie has conducted Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials. Preliminary data from these trials suggest improvements in cognition and biomarkers, supporting further trials to evaluate its potential as a therapy for the six million Americans living with AD.

**About BioVie Inc.**


BioVie Inc. (NASDAQ: BIVI) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing therapies for neurological disorders and advanced liver disease. Its lead investigational drug candidate, bezisterim (NE3107), targets neuroinflammation and insulin resistance, which are believed to be key drivers of Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease. Bezisterim is also being studied for Long COVID, where persistent inflammation is thought to underlie symptoms such as brain fog and fatigue.


In liver disease, BioVie is advancing BIV201, a continuous infusion of terlipressin treatment that has received FDA Orphan and Fast Track designations. The active agent is approved in the U.S. and in about 40 countries for related complications of advanced liver cirrhosis, and the Company plans to study BIV201 in a Phase 3 trial for the reduction of further decompensation in patients with cirrhosis and ascites.
